description: methodology 1.3 — the ACTIVATION WIDTH the trunk sees. The full store width ships (512 channels, standardized and NOT rotated), so there is no wider arm and the question is one-sided: what each narrower joint-PCA width costs on held-out-PROBLEM likelihood against the shipped full width, and whether that cost is monotone in the width. The arms sweep 64 / 128 / 256 / 512, `shipped512` being the shipped width and the baseline every contrast is taken against; it declares pca_dim 512 explicitly so the record names the width it ran at. THE SHIPPED ARM DIFFERS FROM THE NARROWER ONES IN TWO WAYS AT ONCE: it keeps every channel AND it is unrotated, whereas a narrower arm is the leading components of a joint PCA of the same channels. A rotated full-width arm does not exist (a width at or above the store's means no rotation), so the panel cannot separate truncation from rotation and a cost here is the cost of the narrower REPRESENTATION as a whole. EVERY ARM HOLDS OUT WHOLE PROBLEMS (stop_unit=problem) in place of the shipped row split, because a claim about the FEATURE side cannot be scored on the row split: that split leaves every problem partly trained, whereas a held-out problem's parameters come from the feature trunk alone, which is exactly what a width is being judged on. Such an arm is uncalibrated and scored as trained. EVERY ARM RUNS AT TWO SEEDS. Within one seed the arms hold aside the SAME problems, so a cross-arm delta is paired; the seeds differ BY DESIGN and therefore hold aside different problems, so no cross-seed likelihood delta is quotable from this panel — what the second seed buys is a second independent paired estimate, and agreement in SIGN between the two is what a contrast is quoted on. The seed also re-rolls the randomized PCA basis of the narrower arms and is inert on the shipped one's feature side. THIS PANEL STOPS AT THE FIT: no rank mapping is re-derived and no motif reading re-counted, so nothing measured here covers what a width does downstream of the likelihood.
